papers.title_in_file: Kirkwood-Dirac Nonpositivity Is a Necessary Resource for Quantum Computing
papers.what_it_is: A letter extending the rebit DGBR quasiprobability to a Z2n Kirkwood-Dirac distribution, constructing two-qubit bound-magic states and defining the KD mana as a resource monotone.

assertions.value: The paper defines the DGBR model as: initialization of qubits in CSS states; applications of H on all qubits, CNOT and Pauli strings; measurement of any qubit in the computational basis, with previous outcomes allowed to determine future operations adaptively.
quotes: Definition 1 (DGBR model). The DGBR model includes the following operations:
• Initialization of qubits in CSS states.
Previous measurement outcomes may determine future operations adaptively.

assertions.value: The authors choose the group G to be Z2 to the power n with addition modulo 2, with the computational basis as basis A and the Pauli-X eigenbasis built from characters as basis B, giving the Z2n-KD distribution Q(g,chi)(rho) = Tr(B(g,chi) rho).
quotes: We have chosen for G to be Z2n, which leads to the aforementioned A and B choices.
With respect to this A and B, a state ρ is represented by the KD distribution
The Z2n-KD distribution has the phase-point operators
assertions.certainty_reason: Setup and definition in the main text.

assertions.value: The authors state that the KD distribution is informationally complete on H, unlike the DGBR distribution, and that a state rho is a rebit state if and only if its KD distribution is real, so all KD-positive states are rebit states.
quotes: this KD distribution is informationally complete on H [28], unlike the DGBR distribution.
ρ is a rebit state if and only if Qg,χ(ρ) is real. Hence, all KD-positive states are rebit states.
assertions.reader_inference: The informational completeness is attributed to Ref. [28]; the rebit equivalence is argued in one line from realness of the overlaps.

assertions.value: The paper states the overlap formula giving outcome probabilities Tr(E_l rho) as a sum over g,chi of the KD representation of the measurement times the KD distribution of the state, citing Refs. [28, 31].
quotes: The outcome probabilities follow from the overlap formula [28, 31]

assertions.value: The paper states the real part of the Z2n-KD distribution equals the DGBR distribution. The proof shows the DGBR phase-point operators are the hermitianization of the KD phase-point operators and evaluates the trace using that matrix elements of the KD point operators are real and that the real and imaginary parts of rho are symmetric and antisymmetric.
assertions.anchor: Theorem 1.1, p.3; Lemma 3 and Lemma 4, Supp. Note II
quotes: 1. (DGBR connection) The real part of the Zn2 -KD distribution [63] equals the DGBR distribution:
Lemma 4 (DGBR Connection). Let Wg,χ and Qg,χ denote the DGBR distribution and the Zn2 -KD distribution respectively. Then Re [Qg,χ(ρ)] = Wg,χ(ρ).
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated and proved in Supp. Note II.

assertions.value: The authors conclude from Theorem 1.1 that the DGBR-positive rebit states are the KD-positive states.
quotes: By Theorem 1.1, the DGBR-positive rebit states are the KD-positive states.
assertions.certainty_reason: Direct consequence of Theorem 1.1 as stated.

assertions.value: The paper states (Hudson's theorem) that any given pure state is Z2n-KD-positive if and only if it is a CSS state. The proof builds on a cited result that pure KD-positive states for any finite Abelian group have the form P(g,chi) applied to a uniform superposition over a subgroup H, and shows their maximal stabilizing group is generated by Z strings and X strings, and that every CSS state has this form.
assertions.anchor: Theorem 1.2, p.3; Lemma 5, Supp. Note III
quotes: 2. (Hudson’s theorem) Any given pure state is Z2n-KDpositive if and only if it is a CSS state.
Lemma 5 (Hudson’s Theorem for the Zn2 -KD Distribution). Let |ψ⟩ ∈ H. |ψ⟩ is KD positive if and only if |ψ⟩ is a CSS state.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated and proved in Supp. Note III, relying on Ref. [31] for the pure-state form.
assertions.reader_inference: The proof depends on the cited characterization of pure KD-positive states in Ref. [31].

assertions.value: The paper states the Z2n-KD distribution is covariant under the DGBR operations: Pauli strings shift the indices, the Hadamard on all qubits swaps g and chi (with complex conjugation), and CNOT acts on the indices by the matrices A_ct and B_ct. The Pauli-string relation follows from a cited result, and the Hadamard and CNOT relations are proved by direct evaluation.
assertions.anchor: Theorem 1.3, p.3; Lemma 6, Supp. Note IV
quotes: 3. (Covariance) The Zn2 -KD distribution is covariant with respect to the DGBR operations
The covariance relation (10) follows from Eq. (29) in Ref. [31].
Lemma 6 (Covariance). The Zn2 -KD distribution obeys the following covariance relationships:
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated and proved in Supp. Note IV.

assertions.value: Theorem 1.4: the Z2n-KD distribution of a tensor product of states factorizes into the product of the KD distributions; the authors state it follows from direct calculation.
quotes: 4. (Products) Let H factorize as the tensor product
Theorem 1.4 follows from direct calculation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated; proof given only as direct calculation.

assertions.value: The authors state that every KD-positive state is DGBR-positive, and so the DGBR model enhanced by any Z2n-KD-positive input state is efficiently classically simulable; they restate the simulation algorithm in KD terms in Supp. Note V.
quotes: Theorem 1.1 implies that every KD-positive state is DGBR-positive. As DGBR-positive input states are efficiently classically simulable, so is the DGBR model enhanced by any Z2n-KD-positive input state ρinput.
assertions.certainty_reason: Follows from Theorem 1.1 and the cited DGBR simulability.

assertions.value: The paper gives a phase-space simulation algorithm for DGBR circuits with KD-positive input that the authors say runs in linear time. The paper proves that if rho is KD positive and one can sample efficiently from Q(rho), an efficient classical algorithm samples the same output distribution as the circuit; the proof is by induction using a measurement-update lemma.
assertions.anchor: Algorithm 1, Lemma 7, Theorem 8, Supp. Note V
quotes: This algorithm runs in linear time.

Theorem 8. Let C be a DGBR circuit with input state ρ. If ρ is KD positive and we can sample efficiently from Q(ρ), then there exists an efficient classical algorithm that samples from the same probability distribution as the quantum circuit.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 8 stated with its condition (efficient sampling from Q) and proved in Supp. Note V.
assertions.reader_inference: Efficiency depends on being able to sample from Q(rho) efficiently, which the paper assumes in Theorem 8.

assertions.value: The authors state that the single-qubit Z2-KD-positive states are the mixtures of the computational and Pauli-X basis projectors (citing Theorem 1.1.i of Ref. [29]), these are the single-qubit rebit-stabilizer states, and so for tensor products of single-rebit inputs the KD distribution cannot identify single-qubit bound-magic states within the DGBR model.
quotes: The single-qubit Z2-KD-positive states are the mixtures of |g(z)⟩ ⟨g(z)| and |χ(x)⟩ ⟨χ(x)| (Theorem 1.1.i of Ref. [29]).
Thus, the Zn2 -KD distribution cannot identify single-qubit bound magic states within the DGBR model.
assertions.reader_inference: The single-qubit characterization is cited from Ref. [29].

assertions.value: The paper shows that the two-qubit state rho_lambda = I/4 + lambda F, is KD-positive for lambda in [0, 1/(4 + 8 sqrt 2)], lies outside the facet Tr(rho F) <= 1 for lambda > 1/20, and hence is a two-qubit bound-magic state relative to the DGBR model for lambda in (1/20, 1/(4 + 8 sqrt 2)].
quotes: Every state ρ on the CSS-and-rebit-stabilizer facet’s inner side satisfies Tr(ρF ) ≤ 1.
If λ > 1/20, then Tr(F ρλ) > 1,√so ρλ lies outside the facet.
Thus, if λ ∈ (1/20, 1/(4 + 8 2)], ρλ is a twoqubit bound-magic state relative to the DGBR model.
we show that ρλ is KD-positive if λ ∈ [0, 1/(4 + 8 2)]
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytical construction in Supp. Note VI.
assertions.reader_inference: Outside the rebit stabilizer polytope, which contains all real stabilizer mixtures, implies magic; this step is in Supp. Note VI.

assertions.value: In the supplement the authors give the KD distribution of rho_lambda (Eq. S31), state it is KD positive for lambda in [-1/12, 1/12], and find rho_lambda is positive semidefinite for lambda in [0, 1/(4 + 8 sqrt 2)] because the minimal eigenvalue of F is stated as -1 - 2 sqrt 2, a stronger requirement than KD positivity.
quotes: ρλ therefore is a KD positive operator for λ ∈ [−1/12, 1/12].
This is a stronger requirement than KD-positivity, so we find that ρλ is a KD positive state for λ ∈ [0, 1/(4 + 8 2)].
assertions.certainty_reason: Computation stated in Supp. Note VI.

assertions.value: The supplement reports that for all 24 rebit stabilizer states on 2 qubits and all 20 CSS states on 2 qubits Tr(rho F) <= 1, with the inequality tight for at least 9 states in each case, so it defines a facet of both polytopes.
quotes: For all 24 rebit stabilizer states on 2 qubits and for all 20 CSS states on 2 qubits, Tr(ρF ) ≤ 1.
The inequality is tight for at least 9 states in each case.

assertions.value: Using the cdd polytope package, the authors report that the rebit stabilizer polytope has 120 facets and the CSS polytope has 40 facets, and that exactly 24 facets coincide. They report for every shared facet lambda_KD+ = 0.083, lambda_SD = 0.065 and lambda_magic = 0.050, and conclude bound states exist above every shared facet.
quotes: We find that the rebit stabilizer polytope has 120 facets and the CSS polytope has 40 facets.
Between these two sets of facets, exactly 24 facets coincide.
For every shared facet, we find λKD+ = 0.083, λSD = 0.065 and λmagic = 0.050.
assertions.reader_inference: The main text says bound-magic states exist above each of 20 shared facets, while Supp. Note VII reports 24 coinciding facets; the paper does not reconcile the two numbers.

assertions.value: The main text states that similar bound-magic states exist above each of the 20 facets shared by the CSS polytope and the rebit-stabilizer polytope, and that the claim is proved in Supp. Note VII using cdd.
quotes: Similar bound-magic states exist above each of the 20 facets shared by the CSS polytope and the rebit-stabilizer polytope.
assertions.reader_inference: Conflicts with the 24 coinciding facets reported in Supp. Note VII.

assertions.value: The paper argues bound-magic states exist for every number of qubits greater than 2 (and exotic KD-positive states likewise), by tensoring a KD-positive single-qubit state with rho_lambda and using that partial trace of a stabilizer mixture is a stabilizer mixture.
quotes: Hence bound-magic states exist for every number > 2 of qubits.
σ⊗(n−2) ⊗ ρλ is KD-positive by Theorem 1.4.
assertions.certainty_reason: Argument given in the main text from Theorem 1.4 and a cited partial-trace property.
assertions.reader_inference: The main text says 'every number > 2' while elsewhere says 2-qubit states exist; the construction as written covers n at least 2 using rho_lambda itself.

assertions.value: The authors report, from sampling 1 billion random two-qubit states, relative volumes (Hilbert-Schmidt measure) of 1.5614(5) % stabilizer and KD-positive, 2.9753(5) % stabilizer and KD-nonpositive, 0.6868(3) % magic and KD-positive (bound), and 94.7766(6) % magic and KD-nonpositive.
assertions.anchor: Table I, p.5; Supp. Note VIII
quotes: Stabilizer & KD-positive
Magic & KD-positive (bound) DGBR 0.6868(3) %
sampling 1 billion random quantum states from the space D((R2)⊗2).
assertions.reader_inference: The states are sampled from real (rebit) two-qubit density matrices via the real Ginibre ensemble, so the percentages are volumes within the two-rebit state space.

assertions.value: The authors state approximately 0.69 % of the 2-rebit states are KD-positive bound-magic states, and that this increases the known set of efficiently classically simulable states by 15 %.
quotes: Approximately 0.69 % of the 2-rebit states are KD-positive bound-magic states. This result increases the known set of efficiently classically simulable states by 15 %.
assertions.reader_inference: 0.6868 divided by (1.5614 + 2.9753) is about 0.151, consistent with the 15 % claim.

assertions.value: The supplement states the random rebit states are generated by the real Ginibre ensemble (A A transpose normalized by its trace), that this gives uniform sampling under the Hilbert-Schmidt measure as established in a cited reference, and that classifying 1 billion 2-qubit states took approximately 3.5 days on an Intel Core i9-13900K.
quotes: To ensure unbiased sampling, we generate random rebit density matrices using the real Ginibre ensemble.
Sampling and state classifying 1 billion 2-qubit states took approximately 3.5 days on a x86 64 processor with 24 physical cores and 32 logical CPUs on Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900K.

assertions.value: The authors expect the relative volume of bound-magic states to vanish as n goes to infinity, and argue this does not prevent the algorithm from simulating reasonable DGBR models in which tensor products of k-qubit states are injected with k bounded by a fixed n-independent number.
quotes: We expect the bound-magic states’ relative volume to vanish as n → ∞.
one injects tensor products of k-qubit states, with k bounded by a fixed n-independent number.

assertions.value: The authors define the KD mana as the logarithm of the sum over g,chi of the absolute values of the KD distribution entries, M(rho) = log sum |Q(g,chi)(rho)|, as a measure of KD nonpositivity, within a resource theory whose free states are CSS mixtures and whose free operations are those of the DGBR model.
quotes: The free states are the CSS mixtures, and the free operations are those in the DGBR model.
M(ρ) quantifies the nonpositivity in Qg,χ(ρ).
assertions.certainty_reason: Definition of the measure and the resource theory.

assertions.value: The paper states the KD mana is faithful (zero if and only if rho is KD-positive), additive under tensor products, and nonincreasing under the free operations. Each property is proved in the supplement, with monotonicity covering unitaries, computational-basis measurement, CSS state appending and partial trace.
assertions.anchor: Theorem 2, p.5; Lemmas 9-11, Supp. Note IX
quotes: 1. (Faithfulness) M(ρ) = 0 if and only if ρ is KDpositive.
3. (Monotone) M is nonincreasing under the free operations.
Lemma 11. M is nonincreasing under the free operations and is thus a monotone.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 2 stated and proved in Supp. Note IX.

assertions.value: Corollary 1: any procedure with a nonzero probability of mapping m copies of rho to n copies of sigma requires m greater than n M(sigma) / M(rho) copies of rho on average over trials. The main text gives no separate proof of the corollary.
quotes: Corollary 1. Consider any procedure that has a nonzero probability of mapping ρ⊗m to σ⊗n. The procedure requires m > nM(σ)/M(ρ) copies of ρ, on average over trials.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as a corollary of Theorem 2; the statement and its conditions are quoted, but no proof text is given.
assertions.reader_inference: The statement says 'nonzero probability' and 'on average'; the paper does not show how these follow from a monotone that is shown nonincreasing only under the free operations.

assertions.value: The authors report KD mana values M(|A><A|) = 0.473 and M(|B><B|) = 0.870 for two states |A> and |B>, which when added to the DGBR model give universal quantum computation (a cited result).
quotes: The states |A⟩ and |B⟩ have nonzero KD mana [M(|A⟩ ⟨A|)=0.473 and M(|B⟩ ⟨B|)=0.870].
can perform universal quantum computation [8].

assertions.value: The authors conclude that KD nonpositivity is a necessary resource for quantum advantages in the DGBR model enhanced by arbitrary input states, and that the KD mana provides an easy-to-calculate bound on the rate of state conversion.
quotes: Our work shows that KD nonpositivity is a necessary resource for quantum advantages in the DGBR model enhanced by arbitrary input states.
The KD mana provides an easy-to-calculate bound on the rate of state conversion.
assertions.reader_inference: The scope is the DGBR model; the title states the result for quantum computing in general, which rests on the universality of the augmented DGBR model.

assertions.value: The paper states that the DGBR model augmented with the one- and two-rebit states is universal and can efficiently simulate the quantum-computation-by-state-injection model and vice versa, and by the quantum extended Church-Turing hypothesis has the same computational power as any physical quantum computer.
quotes: Consider augmenting the DGBR model with the one-
and two-rebit states. The augmented model is univer-
by-state-injection model and vice versa.
assertions.reader_inference: Rests on Ref. [8] and on the extended Church-Turing hypothesis, which is a hypothesis.

assertions.value: The authors state their construction answers the open question of whether even-dimensional Hilbert spaces support bound-magic states, noting that Campbell et al. showed standard protocols cannot distill all qubit magic states but the proof does not govern all distillation protocols.
quotes: Our construction answers and extends beyond an open question: do even-dimensional Hilbert spaces support bound-magic states?
The proof does not govern all distillation protocols, however.

assertions.value: The authors state that the bound-magic states are relative to the DGBR model, which Gottesman-Knill includes; that the KD distribution is one instance of a broader class; and that a natural next step is to combine the algorithm with the dynamically-updated quasiprobability scheme of Park et al. [12] to potentially enlarge the bound-magic set or reach nonreal states.
quotes: Although the Gottesman–Knill model includes our model, ours becomes universal if augmented by certain distillable-magic states [8].
A natural next step combines our algorithm with the dynamically-updatedquasiprobability scheme of Park et al. [12], potentially enlarging the bound-magic set or reaching nonreal states.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' stated scope and next step.

assertions.value: The paper states that classical algorithms can efficiently simulate the Gottesman-Knill model, and consequently magic states, meaning states that are not mixtures of stabilizer states, are necessary for quantum advantages (citing Ref. [2]).
quotes: Classical algorithms can simulate the Gottesman-Knill model efficiently [3, 4]. Consequently, magic states—states that are not mixtures of stabilizer states—are necessary for quantum advantages [2].

assertions.value: The paper defines a bound-magic state, relative to a model, as a magic state that still yields a classically efficiently simulable model when added to that model, and states that every positive state that is not a mixture of stabilizer states is a bound-magic state.
quotes: bound-magic states—magic states that still yield a classically efficiently simulable
Every positive state, if not a mixture of stabilizer states, is a boundmagic state.
